Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S2-01] Plan the chapter's videos from the chapter map: first one short 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video (5-8 minutes) that teaches the chapter's prerequisites, then the topic videos in teaching order. Narration is 6-8 minutes per book page (Navin, 23 October 2026; the 14-page tissue chapter about 85-110 minutes of topic videos, plus the prerequisite video): each topic video gets the share of the pages its items come from, and a very dense page may go up to 25% over when the plan says why. Understanding (Section 1) and the chapter map have no time limit.
[S2-02] Write a spoken teacher script in beats with a natural teacher flow. Stories and analogies only where they genuinely help that topic. Every item the book teaches is taught and every teacher question answered from the book is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the time allows. Cut repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[S2-03] Prerequisites are only what this chapter directly needs, never a prerequisite of a prerequisite. They are taught, not named, in the chapter's 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video, each with a simple explanation and an example; a topic video may remind of them in at most 2 beats.
[S2-04] Spoken Hinglish the way Navin teaches, in mixed script (Navin, 21 and 23 October 2026): Hindi words in Devanagari, English words, above all the book's technical terms, in Roman exactly as the book spells them, as in 'आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे'; a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical; not in BIE's everyday word list rulebook/simple_hindi.json) gets its English word in brackets right after it, as in 'सतह (surface)'; the screen and subtitles show the bracket and the voice says 'सतह, यानी surface'. Never a bracket after an everyday word or inside an idiom or a fixed phrase ('आम तौर पर', not 'आम तौर (usually) पर'; 'नहीं के बराबर', not 'नहीं के बराबर (equal to)'). Never an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman. Numbers as digits; short spoken sentences addressed to one student; questions to the student and natural pauses; no reading out of lists.
[S2-05] Every beat states which chapter-map items it covers and which teacher questions it answers, and those claims must be true: the beat really explains that item and really answers that question.
[S2-06] Teach every part of a video through the universal frame (what the process is, how it works, when and in what order, under which conditions, in what atmosphere) and through the teaching pattern of its content type, step by step in the pattern's order; every item on the task card is really taught, none only named.
[S2-07] Open every book line in the script, never read it out (Navin, 24 October 2026). A new topic opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any book line the beat carries at least one of: the term's plain meaning with 'yaani' and an everyday image, a why step from a need, an example or the place. Speak complete sentences, not clipped notes. A classification is taught as a family: the overview tree, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence), then the members compared and a memory trick. A pattern step may be skipped only with a stated reason; one recap per part and one closing recap.
[S2-08] Apply first, name after (Navin, 27 October 2026): in an economics script a concept's real-world example runs BEFORE the beat that names the term: the example beats carry the example's numbers (₹50 → ₹65, buyers 2 → 12 → 3) and walk the mechanism step by step; then the term ('isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain'), then the book's definition, then one line on where the learner meets it in real life. The example is the one Section 1 chose for the item (its place, actors, goods, numbers), economically correct and at the learner's level. The numbers are said the way a teacher tells what happened ('pehle aapke paas 500 rupaye the, kiraane ke 100 diye, ab 400 bache'), never as a state report (S2-09). The term is not named before the example by any teaching beat of the same concept either (a sister part may not explain 'the UPI route' before the ₹100 kirana payment runs; a hook or a question to the student may ask about it): BIE's code sends such a script back.
[S2-09] Complete teacher sentences (Navin's verdict on Money v1, 29 October 2026: 'teacher ki naration uske sentence aise poore ho ki banawati na lage aur cheejen samjhane ki process us par depend hai to unka complete tarike se istemal hona jaruri hai'): the narration tells what happened in full, natural sentences; a story's numbers are said conversationally ('pehle aapke paas 500 rupaye the, kiraane ke 100 diye, ab 400 bache'), never as a ledger's state report ('cash ₹500 से ₹400 हुआ', 'savings ₹0 से ₹500 हुईं'). BIE's code sends such a beat back.
[S2-10] Outside facts carry their dated source (the Money lesson resume -d, 29 October 2026, v10: operational descriptions of UPI, NEFT, RTGS and IMPS added real Indian banking knowledge beyond the book without a dated source): for a competitive-exam learner (level upsc_pcs), a teaching beat whose basis is outside the book, or mixed and naming an institution or system that none of its book lines names, carries its source with its year in `source` ('RBI, NEFT FAQ, 2023'); a story, example, hook, analogy or question needs none; a beat whose facts the book line says has basis 'book'. BIE's code sends such a beat back; the review page lists the outside beats with their sources.
[W-01] The narration never points at the book: no 'book के अनुसार', 'किताब कहती है', 'book says', 'page पर', 'textbook', 'NCERT' or any wording of that family (the list in this file, 'wording'). BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the overview tree first: the basis of division and every member named. 2) every member in the same slots: layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence. 3) the members compared side by side, the most confused pair named directly. 4) a memory trick for the family.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-29.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- Open with a question on something visible (every new topic and every new family member): Skin aur stomach, kidney ke upar ek outer layer hai ki nahi? Yeh kis se bani hai? — phir naam: epithelial tissue.
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Contrast with the neighbour (members of one family, and what the exam confuses): Simple epithelium ka kaam protection nahi, woh compound ka hai. Zyada layers = pathogen andar nahi aata.
- Ask and repeat the key word (the one word the learner must keep): Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular.
- Exam memory beats by level (after the understanding, by the level profile): Yaad rakhna: brush border PCT mein. Doosre naam: pavement, tessellated. M2B = muscle to bone = tendon, B2B = bone to bone = ligament.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.

Video v14: Cross-border payments, polymer notes और cryptocurrency
Goal: Learner Project Nexus की जरूरत, leadership, participating systems और country–system matching समझेगा; polymer notes के material–durability claims और cryptocurrency के distributed ownership records को fiat तथा CBDC से अलग करेगा।
Opening hook: अपने देश में payment तुरंत हो जाता है—दूसरे देश के fast-payment system तक पहुँचने में अलग समस्या क्यों आती है?
Story or analogy: पहले national payment systems को जोड़ने की जरूरत से Nexus का mechanism खुलेगा। फिर स्पष्ट topic transition के साथ 3 अलग बदलाव रखेंगे: payment connectivity, note का material और ownership record की व्यवस्था। Polymer तथा crypto को एक जैसी monetary category नहीं बताएँगे।
Planned minutes: 8
Narration time (S2-01): 6.6-8.8 minutes, about 858-1144 spoken words (BIE counts 130 words a minute)
Prerequisites already taught in the prerequisite video (remind of one in at most 2 beats): Purchases, prices, debts and payments due later; Bank balances, deposits, loans and interest; Denominations, monetary arithmetic, percentages and minimum–maximum limits; Purchasing power, inflation, scarcity and liquidity; Central bank, commercial bank, government treasury and bank-to-bank settlement; Foreign currencies, exchange rates, reserves and demand–supply changes; Chronological reading: BCE/CE, centuries, dynasties and law versus implementation dates; Digital instructions, identity authentication, ledgers and payment interfaces
Open every book line (S2-07): a question about something the learner can see, then the name; every term opened: its plain meaning with 'yaani' and one everyday image (the word root where it helps); the why, starting from a need or a problem, one link at a time; an example or the place, by a zoom from the organ or the thing the learner knows; the consequence: what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea; the contrast: what it is not, and what the exam confuses it with; the memory beat by level: the exam's 'yaad rakhna', the other names, the trick.

beats.say: Domestic payment तुरंत है; विदेश भेजना मुश्किल क्यों?
beats.on_screen: Connectivity → material → ownership: three different changes.

beats.say: Singapore में relative को hypothetical ₹10,000 भेजने हैं। Committed principal ₹0 से ₹10,000 हुआ; UPI Indian हिस्सा संभालेगा।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical intended design, not live corridor: ₹0 → ₹10,000 principal; UPI.

beats.say: Connection PayNow तक instruction पहुँचाएगा। Receipt Singapore dollars में होगी; conversion और applicable charges अलग रहेंगे।
beats.on_screen: UPI → intended connection → PayNow; no exchange rate or fees assumed.

beats.say: यह Project Nexus है; Bank for International Settlements, यानी BIS का Innovation Hub इसे lead करता है।
beats.on_screen: Nexus leadership: BIS Innovation Hub.

beats.say: Multilateral यानी कई देश; cross-border यानी देशों के बीच payments। यह national fast payment systems, यानी FPS, जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Several countries; separate national FPS connected across borders.

beats.say: UPI और PayNow अलग रहते हैं; connection उन्हें एक domestic system या एक currency नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Connect ≠ replace; currencies remain distinct.

beats.say: Remittance में Nexus याद करो: अलग national FPS साथ काम करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Separate FPS working together.

beats.say: विदेश भेजना दुकान के UPI जैसा आसान हो? यही objective है, identical fees या time की guarantee नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Domestic UPI ease is the objective, not guaranteed performance.

beats.say: India से कौन? UPI founding participant है, यानी शुरुआत के group में है; leader नहीं।
beats.on_screen: India—UPI; one founding participant. Leader: BIS Innovation Hub.

beats.say: Singapore और Malaysia में कौन? Singapore–PayNow और Malaysia–DuitNow हैं; Now समान होने से देश समान नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Country–system matching: Singapore—PayNow; Malaysia—DuitNow. Highlight each complete pair.

beats.say: Philippines और Thailand में? Philippines–InstaPay और Thailand–PromptPay हैं; Pay देखकर interchange मत करना।
beats.on_screen: Country–system matching: Philippines—InstaPay; Thailand—PromptPay. Highlight each complete pair.

beats.say: अपने UPI जैसा national system सोचो: यहाँ 5 systems हैं, एक के 5 नाम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Five distinct national systems.

beats.say: ये Nexus के country–system associations का undated snapshot हैं, live corridors का प्रमाण नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Context: Project Nexus country–system associations. Reference date not supplied; names do not establish operational corridors, fees or launch dates.

beats.say: Matching trap याद रखो: Singapore–PayNow, Thailand–PromptPay; UPI participant है, leader नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Five-pair table; emphasize PayNow versus PromptPay.

beats.say: विदेश भेजना दुकान के UPI जैसा आसान हो? यही objective है, identical fees या time की guarantee नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Domestic UPI ease is the objective, not guaranteed performance.

beats.say: India से कौन? UPI founding participant है, यानी शुरुआत के group में है; leader नहीं।
beats.on_screen: India—UPI; one founding participant. Leader: BIS Innovation Hub.

beats.say: Singapore और Malaysia में कौन? Singapore–PayNow और Malaysia–DuitNow हैं; Now समान होने से देश समान नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Country–system matching: Singapore—PayNow; Malaysia—DuitNow. Highlight each complete pair.

beats.say: Philippines और Thailand में? Philippines–InstaPay और Thailand–PromptPay हैं; Pay देखकर interchange मत करना।
beats.on_screen: Country–system matching: Philippines—InstaPay; Thailand—PromptPay. Highlight each complete pair.

beats.say: अपने UPI जैसा national system सोचो: यहाँ 5 systems हैं, एक के 5 नाम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Five distinct national systems.

beats.say: Country–system जोड़ी पहचानो; इससे live corridor साबित नहीं होता।
beats.on_screen: Country–system association ≠ operational corridor.

beats.say: Matching trap याद रखो: Singapore–PayNow, Thailand–PromptPay; UPI participant है, leader नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Five-pair table; emphasize PayNow versus PromptPay.

beats.say: खर्च क्यों बढ़े? Hypothetical ₹10,000 principal, अलग ₹100 fee, 1 working day मानो; outlay ₹10,100 है।
beats.on_screen: Teaching assumptions, not bank quotes: ₹10,000 + ₹100; 1 working day.

beats.say: बीच का bank ₹50 और 1 working day जोड़ता है। Fee ₹150, outlay ₹10,150, समय 2 working days हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Principal unchanged at ₹10,000; charges paid separately; no conversion assumed.

beats.say: ये correspondent banks payment आगे पहुँचाते हैं। Direct arrangement न हो, तो बीच की handling खर्च और समय बढ़ा सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Intermediary handling → possible charges and delay.

beats.say: ₹1000 instruction भेजने के लिए connections कैसे बनाएँ? Illustrative model में Indian team ने 4 partners के अलग designs बनाए; फिर 1 shared design अपनाया। 3 partners होते, तो भी उनके 3 designs की जगह यही 1 तरीका चलता।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical integration model, not a live corridor: ₹1000 instruction; 4 partner designs → 1 shared design. Three-partner variant: 3 → 1.

beats.say: यही Nexus का standardized connection है: हर partner का अलग link नहीं बनाना पड़ता; counts illustrative हैं।
beats.on_screen: Shared rules reduce repeated bilateral integration, not actual software counts.

beats.say: हर transfer की chain समान नहीं; standardization conversion, कानून या responsibilities नहीं मिटाता।
beats.on_screen: Usually ≠ always; cross-border obligations remain.

beats.say: Handling खर्च बढ़ा सकती है; shared standard connection-work घटाता है।
beats.on_screen: Payment friction → need for shared connectivity.

beats.say: ₹10 note की sheet बदले तो value बदलेगी? Hypothetically 1 authorized BOPP note लो; सामान ₹10 का ही है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical purchase: polymer notes 0 → 1; cotton-paper replaced, value ₹10 unchanged. Not rollout evidence.

beats.say: यह polymer note है: substrate यानी आधार-sheet cotton-based paper नहीं, security-grade Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene, यानी BOPP है।
beats.on_screen: Cotton-based paper versus security-grade BOPP substrate.

beats.say: Biaxially oriented यानी बनाते समय film को लंबाई-चौड़ाई जैसी 2 दिशाओं में खींचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Two perpendicular stretching arrows.

beats.say: Ordinary plastic पर ₹10 लिखना authorized banknote बनाना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Non-example: marked ordinary plastic.

beats.say: आगे durability में यही material-change काम आएगा।
beats.on_screen: Material changes, not face value; next: durability.

beats.say: Plastic और banknote समान हैं? Material-family मिल सकती है; banknote specially engineered होता है।
beats.on_screen: Common material family; different engineered purpose.

beats.say: Embedded security यानी बनावट में पहचान, जैसे ID की निशानी। Paper notes भी साथ चलेंगे, जैसे wallet में पुराने-नए designs।
beats.on_screen: Built-in authenticity identification; paper and polymer streams remain alongside each other.

beats.say: पहचान imitation पकड़ने में मदद करती है। Coexistence दोनों को चलने देता है; withdrawal एक kind हटाता है।
beats.on_screen: Authenticity checks; coexistence versus withdrawal.

beats.say: Material change को demonetisation मत समझना: existing paper notes बेकार नहीं बताए गए हैं।
beats.on_screen: Material change ≠ invalidation.

beats.say: Engineered note ordinary plastic नहीं; साथ चलना replacement नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Two-row comparison recap.

beats.say: Small notes में किनसे शुरुआत का proposal है? RBI के ₹10, ₹20; lifespan claim up to 4x है।
beats.on_screen: Proposed ₹10, ₹20; up to 4x lifespan.

beats.say: Baseline 1 bar हो, तो upper comparison 4 bars है; 4 extra years नहीं।
beats.on_screen: L versus 4L; no years assigned.

beats.say: Claim का up to upper limit बताता है, हर note का measured result नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Upper limit ≠ exact achieved outcome; claim undated.

beats.say: छोटे notes बार-बार हाथ बदलते हैं; इसलिए wear और replacement की जरूरत जाँचना उपयोगी होगा।
beats.on_screen: Frequent handling → practical durability assessment.

beats.say: Baseline गुणा 4 upper comparison है; denominations ₹10, ₹20 हैं।
beats.on_screen: Upper comparison = baseline × 4; up to, not exact.

beats.say: नई sheet से पहले किसका अनुभव देखें? Introduction और testing अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: International introduction versus Indian testing.

beats.say: Australia ने 1988 में पहले introduce किया। India में 2013 की ₹10 field-trial approval सिर्फ limited testing की हाँ थी।
beats.on_screen: 1988 Australia: first introduction; 2013 India: ₹10 trial approval.

beats.say: Government ने approval दी; असली handling में जाँच से laboratory से छूटी परेशानियाँ मिल सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Government choice: limited real-use test.

beats.say: Event पहचानो: approval से trial completion या nationwide circulation साबित नहीं होती।
beats.on_screen: Approval ≠ completion ≠ national rollout.

beats.say: 50 से ज्यादा countries का इस्तेमाल experience देता है, Indian savings का प्रमाण नहीं।
beats.on_screen: >50 countries: comparative experience, not proof of Indian cost savings.

beats.say: 1988 introduction था; 2013 Indian trial approval थी।
beats.on_screen: 1988 Australia introduction → 2013 Government approval of ₹10 Indian field trial.

beats.say: खराब notes कम हों तो क्या बचेगा? मानो एक period में 100 ₹10 notes खराब हुए; बराबर handling वाले दूसरे period में ज्यादा durable notes में सिर्फ 50 खराब हुए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical equal-period comparison: 100 unfit notes versus 50 under comparable handling; not measured results.

beats.say: Longer life से collection और replacement घटें: यही durability से replacement costs घटाने का उद्देश्य है।
beats.on_screen: Durability → fewer replacements → lower recurring work.

beats.say: दूसरा अलग लक्ष्य counterfeiting कठिन करना है: wear रोकना और imitation रोकना अलग काम हैं।
beats.on_screen: Goals: longer life, harder counterfeiting, lower replacement costs.

beats.say: ये illustrative counts हैं, measured savings नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Illustration ≠ measured savings.

beats.say: Unit production सस्ता होना जरूरी नहीं; कम replacement बचत दे सकता है। Durable भी counterfeit-proof नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Production cost ≠ replacement cost; durable ≠ counterfeit-proof.

beats.say: Durability replacement घटाए; security imitation रोके।
beats.on_screen: Two separate benefit chains; objectives, not guaranteed outcomes.

beats.say: बिना note ownership कैसे बदले? मानो आपके पास 2 units हैं, receiver के पास 0; fees छोड़कर 1 भेजें, तो आपके पास 1 बचेगी, उसे 1 मिलेगी। Validation के बाद linked blocks में record बनेगा।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical transfer; fees ignored: authorize 1 → validate → linked-block record; sender 2 → 1, recipient 0 → 1.

beats.say: यह cryptocurrency है: blockchain से created और stored digital/virtual currency। Blockchain जुड़े blocks का record है, जैसे जुड़े हिसाब-पन्ने।
beats.on_screen: Blockchain: linked blocks containing transaction records.

beats.say: हर phone balance crypto नहीं; wallet transfer की keys संभालता है, literal coins नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Wallet manages cryptographic keys; blockchain maintains transaction records.
beats.source: FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers, 2021

beats.say: Blockchain record official money नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Blockchain technology ≠ official monetary status.

beats.say: Phone पर crypto और Digital Rupee समान लगें? Digital रूप समान, issuer और legal status अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: Cryptocurrency | Digital Rupee: both digital; compare issuer and legal status next.
beats.source: RBI, Concept Note on Central Bank Digital Currency, 2022

beats.say: Crypto private asset है, RBI-issued नहीं; Digital Rupee RBI-issued CBDC है। India में पहला legal tender नहीं, दूसरा है।
beats.on_screen: Cryptocurrency | Digital Rupee. Issuer: private, not RBI | RBI. Indian legal tender: no | yes.
beats.source: RBI, Concept Note on Central Bank Digital Currency, 2022

beats.say: Legal tender यानी payment की देनदारी चुकाने के लिए कानून से मान्यता वाला money; केवल transferable होना यह मान्यता नहीं देता।
beats.on_screen: Legal tender: legally recognized money for discharging payment obligations. Transferability alone is insufficient.
beats.source: RBI, Concept Note on Central Bank Digital Currency, 2022

beats.say: Not legal tender सीधे illegal नहीं; holding, trading और tax अलग सवाल हैं।
beats.on_screen: Legal-tender status, holding/trading rules and taxation are separate questions.
beats.source: Government of India, Ministry of Finance, Rajya Sabha written reply on cryptocurrency, 14 March 2022

beats.say: Crypto private, legal tender नहीं; Digital Rupee RBI का, legal tender है।
beats.on_screen: Difference table: Cryptocurrency | Digital Rupee. Digital: yes | yes. Issuer: private, not RBI | RBI. Indian legal tender: no | yes.
beats.source: RBI, Concept Note on Central Bank Digital Currency, 2022

beats.say: Bank की अकेली copy बिना हिसाब कैसे चले? मानो आपके पास 3 units थीं; fees छोड़कर आपने 1 भेजी, transfer accept हुआ, आपके पास 2 बचीं और receiver को 1 मिली।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical accepted transfer, fees ignored: sender begins with 3; sends 1; retains 2. Recipient begins with 0 and receives 1.

beats.say: इसकी शुरुआत आपके authorization और network computers से हुई।
beats.on_screen: Input: authorized instruction. Place: participating network computers.
beats.source: BIS, Annual Economic Report, Chapter V: Cryptocurrencies—looking beyond the hype, 2018

beats.say: Valid transfer accept हो तो distributed ledger बदले: कई computers की हिसाब-कॉपियों में मिलती entry, bank या government की अकेली copy नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Network rules validate and accept the transfer; matching ownership entries update across participating computers.

beats.say: Update न हो तो वही unit पुराने owner के पास उपलब्ध दिख सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Missing update risks inconsistent ownership and repeated spending.

beats.say: जाँच के बाद entry बदली; आपको 2 बचीं, उसे 1 मिली।
beats.on_screen: Replay: authorize → validate → accept → update holdings.
beats.source: BIS, Annual Economic Report, Chapter V: Cryptocurrencies—looking beyond the hype, 2018

beats.say: Authorize, validate, update: भरोसा network rules पर है।
beats.on_screen: Authorize → validate → distributed ownership update.

beats.say: Banking पर भरोसा क्यों हिले? मानो weak-credit borrower पर $100000 बाकी थे; वह हर महीने $800 देता था, फिर repayment रुक गई।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical US borrower: $100000 outstanding; previously paid $800 monthly, then paid nothing.

beats.say: घर से net $70000 मिले: $30000 shortfall हुआ। कई loans और mortgage-backed claims के losses institutions कमजोर कर सकते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Other recoveries ignored: $100000 − $70000 = $30000 loss.

beats.say: Charges से परेशानी क्यों? Hypothetical ₹100 card sale में ₹1 fee कटे; merchant को ₹99 मिले।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative fee, not actual tariff: ₹100 → ₹99 proceeds.

beats.say: यह subprime distress है: losses से distrust, फिर alternatives में interest हो सकता है। Anarchist groups central authority का विरोध करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Loan losses → financial disruption → possible distrust → interest in alternatives.

beats.say: यह merchant acceptance charge MDR, यानी Merchant Discount Rate, समझाता है: fee से दुकानदार की receipt घटी। E-banking/card charges और interoperability की परेशानी भी motives हैं; interoperability यानी अलग systems साथ काम करें।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical acceptance fee: ₹100 sale − ₹1 fee = ₹99 merchant receipt. MDR: Merchant Discount Rate. Interoperability: systems working together.
beats.source: RBI, Rationalisation of Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) for Debit Card Transactions, 2017; BIS, Annual Economic Report, Chapter III: A blueprint for the future monetary system, 2022

beats.say: कुछ anarchist groups ने USA की 2007 Subprime Crisis से dollar की purchasing power घटने को FIAT MONEY पर distrust का कारण माना। यह दावा है, losses से पक्का नतीजा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Attributed claim: crisis → dollar purchasing-power erosion → fiat distrust. Loan losses do not establish that purchasing-power claim.

beats.say: FIAT MONEY monetary/legal system से चलता है, fixed-gold conversion से नहीं। Purchasing power यानी रकम कितना सामान खरीदे; loan loss इसका घटना साबित नहीं करता।
beats.on_screen: Fiat: monetary/legal backing, not fixed-gold convertibility. Purchasing power: goods and services a sum buys. Loan loss ≠ proof of purchasing-power erosion.
beats.source: Bank of England, Money in the modern economy: an introduction, 2014; Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission, Final Report, 2011

beats.say: Crypto भी risky है; fees और compatibility limits मिटती नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Seeking an alternative does not establish safety, zero fees or universal compatibility.
beats.source: BIS, Annual Economic Report, Chapter III: A blueprint for the future monetary system, 2022

beats.say: Distrust और charges motives हैं, guarantees नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Motivations ≠ guaranteed benefits.

beats.say: Connectivity, material, private records: तीनों अलग रखो।
beats.on_screen: Nexus: payment connectivity | Polymer: note material | Crypto: private ownership records. Next: money supply.

frame.process: Define Nexus as a BIS Innovation Hub-led connection between national fast payment systems.
frame.how: Follow a hypothetical India–Singapore remittance through separate domestic payment legs.
frame.when: Explain the intended arrangement, not an asserted live corridor.
frame.conditions: Currency conversion and applicable charges remain necessary.
frame.atmosphere: A sender in India wants to support a relative in Singapore.

frame.process: Identify the objective, founding participation and five country–system pairs.
frame.how: Associate each country with its own named national system.
frame.when: After defining the initiative and before explaining connection costs.
frame.conditions: Participation is distinct from leadership; ease is an objective.
frame.atmosphere: A country–system matching exercise anchored in familiar UPI payments.

skipped_steps.why: These are associations and an objective, with no formula to build.

frame.process: Explain intermediary costs and the benefit of shared connection standards.
frame.how: Add an illustrative handling stage, then contrast separate interfaces with a shared design.
frame.when: During remittance routing and payment-system integration.
frame.conditions: Fees and delays vary; connection standardization does not abolish currencies or legal requirements.
frame.atmosphere: A bank transfer counter and a payment-integration desk.

frame.process: Define polymer notes by their supporting material.
frame.how: Replace cotton-based paper with security-grade BOPP while retaining face value.
frame.when: A hypothetical authorized note is used in a purchase.
frame.conditions: The example does not establish Indian circulation.
frame.atmosphere: A kirana purchase worth ₹10.

frame.process: Distinguish engineered banknotes from ordinary plastic and coexistence from withdrawal.
frame.how: Compare security design and the treatment of existing paper notes.
frame.when: When interpreting a proposed material change.
frame.conditions: A different substrate alone neither creates a banknote nor cancels existing currency.
frame.atmosphere: A shopkeeper checks notes and keeps valid paper notes in use.

frame.process: Interpret proposed denominations and the lifespan multiplier.
frame.how: Compare a baseline lifespan with an upper-bound multiplier.
frame.when: When assessing the proposed small-denomination introduction.
frame.conditions: Up to 4x is not an exact outcome or four extra years.
frame.atmosphere: Frequently handled ₹10 and ₹20 notes.

frame.process: Place international introduction and Indian trial approval in chronological order.
frame.how: Move from Australia in 1988 to Government approval in 2013.
frame.when: Distinguish introduction, approval and wider adoption.
frame.conditions: Approval is not proof of nationwide circulation; adoption figures have no supplied reference date.
frame.atmosphere: International experience alongside a limited Indian testing proposal.

frame.process: Explain durability, anti-counterfeiting and replacement-cost objectives.
frame.how: Reduce illustrative unfit notes, then separate wear resistance from imitation resistance.
frame.when: Over comparable periods of handling and replacement.
frame.conditions: Illustrative quantities are not measured savings; objectives are not achieved outcomes.
frame.atmosphere: A bank cash counter collecting worn notes.

frame.process: Define cryptocurrency through a blockchain-recorded digital transfer.
frame.how: Track changes in hypothetical holdings and explain linked records.
frame.when: After a transfer is validated.
frame.conditions: Fees are ignored in the illustration; digital form does not establish official monetary status.
frame.atmosphere: Two users transferring a hypothetical digital asset.

frame.process: Separate privately created crypto from RBI-issued digital money.
frame.how: Compare issuer and legal-tender status rather than digital appearance.
frame.when: When classifying an asset as official money or a private asset.
frame.conditions: Absence of legal-tender status alone does not determine legality of holding or trading.
frame.atmosphere: Two digital balances with different institutional status.

frame.process: Explain ownership recording through a distributed ledger.
frame.how: Validate a proposed transfer and update records maintained across participating computers.
frame.when: A valid transfer is accepted under network rules.
frame.conditions: An unaccepted instruction does not establish changed ownership; network details vary.
frame.atmosphere: Several computers maintain a consistent ownership record.

frame.process: Explain distrust and payment grievances as motivations for alternatives.
frame.how: Trace mortgage default to loss, and a merchant fee to lower net receipts.
frame.when: During financial distress or costly and incompatible payment experiences.
frame.conditions: Motivation proves neither crypto safety nor freedom from fees; crisis losses do not prove dollar purchasing-power erosion.
frame.atmosphere: A hypothetical US mortgage lender and an Indian kirana payment counter.

beats.say: Domestic payment तुरंत है; विदेश भेजना मुश्किल क्यों?
beats.on_screen: Connectivity → material → ownership: three different changes.

beats.say: मानो Singapore में relative को भेजने के लिए पहले ₹0 रखे थे; अब ₹10,000 रखे हैं। UPI Indian हिस्सा संभालेगा।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical intended design, not live corridor: ₹0 → ₹10,000 principal; UPI.

beats.say: Connection PayNow तक instruction पहुँचाएगा। Receipt Singapore dollars में होगी; conversion और applicable charges अलग रहेंगे।
beats.on_screen: UPI → intended connection → PayNow; no exchange rate or fees assumed.

beats.say: यह Project Nexus है; Bank for International Settlements, यानी BIS का Innovation Hub इसे lead करता है।
beats.on_screen: Nexus leadership: BIS Innovation Hub.

beats.say: Multilateral यानी कई देश; cross-border यानी देशों के बीच payments। यह national fast payment systems, यानी FPS, जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Several countries; separate national FPS connected across borders.

beats.say: National systems अलग रहते हैं; जोड़ना उन्हें 1 domestic system बनाना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Separate national FPS remain distinct: connect ≠ replace.

beats.say: Remittance में Nexus याद करो: अलग national FPS साथ काम करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Separate FPS working together.

beats.say: विदेश भेजना दुकान के UPI जैसा आसान हो? यही objective है, identical fees या time की guarantee नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Domestic UPI ease is the objective, not guaranteed performance.

beats.say: India से कौन? UPI founding participant है, यानी शुरुआत के group में है; leader नहीं।
beats.on_screen: India—UPI; one founding participant. Leader: BIS Innovation Hub.

beats.say: Singapore और Malaysia में कौन? Singapore–PayNow और Malaysia–DuitNow हैं; Now समान होने से देश समान नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Country–system matching: Singapore—PayNow; Malaysia—DuitNow. Highlight each complete pair.

beats.say: Philippines और Thailand में? Philippines–InstaPay और Thailand–PromptPay हैं; Pay देखकर interchange मत करना।
beats.on_screen: Country–system matching: Philippines—InstaPay; Thailand—PromptPay. Highlight each complete pair.

beats.say: अपने UPI जैसा national system सोचो: यहाँ 5 systems हैं, एक के 5 नाम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Five distinct national systems.

beats.say: Country–system जोड़ी पहचानो; इससे live corridor साबित नहीं होता।
beats.on_screen: Country–system association ≠ operational corridor.

beats.say: Matching trap याद रखो: Singapore–PayNow, Thailand–PromptPay; UPI participant है, leader नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Five-pair table; emphasize PayNow versus PromptPay.

beats.say: खर्च क्यों बढ़े? Hypothetical ₹10,000 principal, अलग ₹100 fee, 1 working day मानो; outlay ₹10,100 है।
beats.on_screen: Teaching assumptions, not bank quotes: ₹10,000 + ₹100; 1 working day.

beats.say: बीच का bank ₹50 और 1 working day जोड़ता है। Fee ₹150, outlay ₹10,150, समय 2 working days हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Principal unchanged at ₹10,000; charges paid separately; no conversion assumed.

beats.say: ये correspondent banks payment आगे पहुँचाते हैं। Direct arrangement न हो, तो बीच की handling खर्च और समय बढ़ा सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Intermediary handling → possible charges and delay.

beats.say: ₹1000 instruction कैसे भेजें? Illustrative model में Indian team ने 4 partner-specific designs की जगह 1 shared design अपनाया। 3 partners होते, तो उनके 3 designs भी इसी 1 तरीके से बदलते।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical integration model, not a live corridor: ₹1000 instruction; 4 partner designs → 1 shared design. Three-partner variant: 3 → 1.

beats.say: यही Nexus का standardized connection है: हर partner का अलग link नहीं बनाना पड़ता; counts illustrative हैं।
beats.on_screen: Shared rules reduce repeated bilateral integration, not actual software counts.

beats.say: हर transfer की chain समान नहीं; standardization conversion, कानून या responsibilities नहीं मिटाता।
beats.on_screen: Usually ≠ always; cross-border obligations remain.

beats.say: Handling खर्च बढ़ा सकती है; shared standard connection-work घटाता है।
beats.on_screen: Payment friction → need for shared connectivity.

beats.say: ₹10 note की sheet बदले तो value बदलेगी? Hypothetically 1 authorized BOPP note लो; सामान ₹10 का ही है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical purchase: polymer notes 0 → 1; cotton-paper replaced, value ₹10 unchanged. Not rollout evidence.

beats.say: यह polymer note है: substrate यानी आधार-sheet cotton-based paper नहीं, security-grade Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene, यानी BOPP है।
beats.on_screen: Cotton-based paper versus security-grade BOPP substrate.

beats.say: Biaxially oriented यानी बनाते समय film को लंबाई-चौड़ाई जैसी 2 दिशाओं में खींचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Two perpendicular stretching arrows.

beats.say: Ordinary plastic पर ₹10 लिखना authorized banknote बनाना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Non-example: marked ordinary plastic.

beats.say: आगे durability में यही material-change काम आएगा।
beats.on_screen: Material changes, not face value; next: durability.

beats.say: Plastic और banknote समान हैं? Material-family मिल सकती है; banknote specially engineered होता है।
beats.on_screen: Common material family; different engineered purpose.

beats.say: Embedded security यानी बनावट में पहचान, जैसे ID की निशानी। Paper notes भी साथ चलेंगे, जैसे wallet में पुराने-नए designs।
beats.on_screen: Built-in authenticity identification; paper and polymer streams remain alongside each other.

beats.say: पहचान imitation पकड़ने में मदद करती है। Coexistence दोनों को चलने देता है; withdrawal एक kind हटाता है।
beats.on_screen: Authenticity checks; coexistence versus withdrawal.

beats.say: Material change को demonetisation मत समझना: existing paper notes बेकार नहीं बताए गए हैं।
beats.on_screen: Material change ≠ invalidation.

beats.say: Engineered note ordinary plastic नहीं; साथ चलना replacement नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Two-row comparison recap.

beats.say: Small notes में किनसे शुरुआत का proposal है? RBI के ₹10, ₹20; lifespan claim up to 4x है।
beats.on_screen: Proposed ₹10, ₹20; up to 4x lifespan.

beats.say: Baseline 1 bar हो, तो upper comparison 4 bars है; 4 extra years नहीं।
beats.on_screen: L versus 4L; no years assigned.

beats.say: Claim का up to upper limit बताता है, हर note का measured result नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Upper limit ≠ exact achieved outcome; claim undated.

beats.say: छोटे notes बार-बार हाथ बदलते हैं; इसलिए wear और replacement की जरूरत जाँचना उपयोगी होगा।
beats.on_screen: Frequent handling → practical durability assessment.

beats.say: Baseline गुणा 4 upper comparison है; denominations ₹10, ₹20 हैं।
beats.on_screen: Upper comparison = baseline × 4; up to, not exact.

beats.say: नई sheet से पहले किसका अनुभव देखें? Introduction और testing अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: International introduction versus Indian testing.

beats.say: Australia ने 1988 में पहले introduce किया। India में 2013 की ₹10 field-trial approval सिर्फ limited testing की हाँ थी।
beats.on_screen: 1988 Australia: first introduction; 2013 India: ₹10 trial approval.

beats.say: Government ने approval दी; असली handling में जाँच से laboratory से छूटी परेशानियाँ मिल सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Government choice: limited real-use test.

beats.say: Event पहचानो: approval से trial completion या nationwide circulation साबित नहीं होती।
beats.on_screen: Approval ≠ completion ≠ national rollout.

beats.say: 50 से ज्यादा countries का इस्तेमाल experience देता है, Indian savings का प्रमाण नहीं।
beats.on_screen: >50 countries: comparative experience, not proof of Indian cost savings.

beats.say: 1988 introduction था; 2013 Indian trial approval थी।
beats.on_screen: 1988 Australia introduction → 2013 Government approval of ₹10 Indian field trial.

beats.say: खराब notes कम हों तो क्या बचेगा? मानो एक period में 100 ₹10 notes खराब हुए; बराबर handling वाले दूसरे period में ज्यादा durable notes में सिर्फ 50 खराब हुए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical equal-period comparison: 100 unfit notes versus 50 under comparable handling; not measured results.

beats.say: Longer life से collection और replacement घटें: यही durability से replacement costs घटाने का उद्देश्य है।
beats.on_screen: Durability → fewer replacements → lower recurring work.

beats.say: दूसरा अलग लक्ष्य counterfeiting कठिन करना है: wear रोकना और imitation रोकना अलग काम हैं।
beats.on_screen: Goals: longer life, harder counterfeiting, lower replacement costs.

beats.say: ये illustrative counts हैं, measured savings नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Illustration ≠ measured savings.

beats.say: Unit production सस्ता होना जरूरी नहीं; कम replacement बचत दे सकता है। Durable भी counterfeit-proof नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Production cost ≠ replacement cost; durable ≠ counterfeit-proof.

beats.say: Durability replacement घटाए; security imitation रोके।
beats.on_screen: Two separate benefit chains; objectives, not guaranteed outcomes.

beats.say: बिना note ownership कैसे बदले? आपके पास 2 units हैं, receiver के पास 0। Fees छोड़कर 1 भेजें: आपको 1 बचेगी, उसे 1 मिलेगी। Validation के बाद linked blocks में record बनेगा।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical transfer; fees ignored: authorize 1 → validate → linked-block record; sender 2 → 1, recipient 0 → 1.

beats.say: यह cryptocurrency है: blockchain से created और stored digital/virtual currency। Blockchain जुड़े blocks का record है, जैसे जुड़े हिसाब-पन्ने।
beats.on_screen: Blockchain: linked blocks containing transaction records.

beats.say: हर phone balance crypto नहीं; wallet transfer की keys संभालता है, literal coins नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Wallet manages cryptographic keys; blockchain maintains transaction records.
beats.source: FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers, 2021

beats.say: Blockchain record official money नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Blockchain technology ≠ official monetary status.

beats.say: Phone पर crypto और Digital Rupee समान लगें? Digital रूप समान, issuer और legal status अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: Cryptocurrency | Digital Rupee: both digital; compare issuer and legal status next.
beats.source: RBI, Concept Note on Central Bank Digital Currency, 2022

beats.say: Crypto private asset है, RBI-issued नहीं; Digital Rupee RBI-issued CBDC है। India में पहला legal tender नहीं, दूसरा है।
beats.on_screen: Cryptocurrency | Digital Rupee. Issuer: private, not RBI | RBI. Indian legal tender: no | yes.
beats.source: RBI, Concept Note on Central Bank Digital Currency, 2022

beats.say: Legal tender यानी कानून से payment चुकाने के लिए स्वीकार किया गया money। केवल transferable होना काफी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Legal tender: legally recognized money for discharging payment obligations. Transferability alone is insufficient.
beats.source: RBI, Concept Note on Central Bank Digital Currency, 2022

beats.say: Not legal tender सीधे illegal नहीं; holding, trading और tax अलग सवाल हैं।
beats.on_screen: Legal-tender status, holding/trading rules and taxation are separate questions.
beats.source: Government of India, Ministry of Finance, Rajya Sabha written reply on cryptocurrency, 14 March 2022

beats.say: Crypto private, legal tender नहीं; Digital Rupee RBI का, legal tender है।
beats.on_screen: Difference table: Cryptocurrency | Digital Rupee. Digital: yes | yes. Issuer: private, not RBI | RBI. Indian legal tender: no | yes.
beats.source: RBI, Concept Note on Central Bank Digital Currency, 2022

beats.say: Bank की अकेली copy बिना हिसाब कैसे चले? मानो आपकी 3 units थीं, receiver की 0। Fees छोड़कर 1 भेजी; transfer accept हुआ, आपको 2 बचीं, उसे 1 मिली।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical accepted transfer, fees ignored: sender begins with 3; sends 1; retains 2. Recipient begins with 0 and receives 1.

beats.say: इसकी शुरुआत आपके authorization और network computers से हुई।
beats.on_screen: Input: authorized instruction. Place: participating network computers.
beats.source: BIS, Annual Economic Report, Chapter V: Cryptocurrencies—looking beyond the hype, 2018

beats.say: Valid transfer accept हो तो distributed ledger बदले: कई computers की हिसाब-कॉपियों में मिलती entry, bank या government की अकेली copy नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Network rules validate and accept the transfer; matching ownership entries update across participating computers.

beats.say: Update न हो तो वही unit पुराने owner के पास उपलब्ध दिख सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Missing update risks inconsistent ownership and repeated spending.

beats.say: जाँच के बाद entry बदली; आपको 2 बचीं, उसे 1 मिली।
beats.on_screen: Replay: authorize → validate → accept → update holdings.
beats.source: BIS, Annual Economic Report, Chapter V: Cryptocurrencies—looking beyond the hype, 2018

beats.say: Authorize, validate, update: भरोसा network rules पर है।
beats.on_screen: Authorize → validate → distributed ownership update.

beats.say: Banking पर भरोसा क्यों हिले? मानो weak-credit borrower पर $100000 बाकी थे; वह हर महीने $800 देता था, फिर repayment रुक गई।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical US borrower: $100000 outstanding; previously paid $800 monthly, then paid nothing.

beats.say: घर से net $70000 मिले: $30000 shortfall हुआ। कई loans और mortgage-backed claims के losses institutions कमजोर कर सकते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Other recoveries ignored: $100000 − $70000 = $30000 loss.

beats.say: Charges से परेशानी क्यों? Hypothetical ₹100 card sale में ₹1 fee कटे; merchant को ₹99 मिले।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative fee, not actual tariff: ₹100 → ₹99 proceeds.

beats.say: यह subprime distress है: losses से distrust, फिर alternatives में interest हो सकता है। Anarchist groups central authority का विरोध करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Loan losses → financial disruption → possible distrust → interest in alternatives.

beats.say: यह merchant acceptance charge MDR, यानी Merchant Discount Rate, समझाता है: fee से दुकानदार की receipt घटी। E-banking/card charges और interoperability की परेशानी भी motives हैं; interoperability यानी अलग systems साथ काम करें।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical acceptance fee: ₹100 sale − ₹1 fee = ₹99 merchant receipt. MDR: Merchant Discount Rate. Interoperability: systems working together.
beats.source: RBI, Rationalisation of Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) for Debit Card Transactions, 2017; BIS, Annual Economic Report, Chapter III: A blueprint for the future monetary system, 2022

beats.say: कुछ anarchist groups ने USA की 2007 Subprime Crisis से dollar की purchasing power घटने को FIAT MONEY पर distrust का कारण माना। यह दावा है, losses से पक्का नतीजा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Attributed claim: crisis → dollar purchasing-power erosion → fiat distrust. Loan losses do not establish that purchasing-power claim.

beats.say: FIAT MONEY monetary/legal system से चलता है, fixed-gold conversion से नहीं। Purchasing power यानी रकम कितना सामान खरीदे; loan loss इसका घटना साबित नहीं करता।
beats.on_screen: Fiat: monetary/legal backing, not fixed-gold convertibility. Purchasing power: goods and services a sum buys. Loan loss ≠ proof of purchasing-power erosion.
beats.source: Bank of England, Money in the modern economy: an introduction, 2014; Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission, Final Report, 2011

beats.say: Crypto भी risky है; fees और compatibility limits मिटती नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Seeking an alternative does not establish safety, zero fees or universal compatibility.
beats.source: BIS, Annual Economic Report, Chapter III: A blueprint for the future monetary system, 2022

beats.say: Distrust और charges motives हैं, guarantees नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Motivations ≠ guaranteed benefits.

beats.say: Connectivity, material, private records: तीनों अलग रखो।
beats.on_screen: Nexus: payment connectivity | Polymer: note material | Crypto: private ownership records. Next: money supply.

notes.about: This video distinguishes payment-system connectivity, banknote material and cryptocurrency ownership records. Most source content is taught through useful numerical examples and explicit exam contrasts.
key_questions: How does Nexus connect separate national payment systems?
What changes with polymer notes, and what does not?
How do distributed records differ from RBI issuance and legal-tender status?
How do charges and incompatible systems motivate interest in alternatives?

decisions.decision: Require a concrete explanation of the interoperability grievance.
decisions.reason: Defining compatibility does not explain how incompatibility obstructs an actual payment.

decisions.decision: Require dated attribution for the manufacturing explanation.
decisions.reason: The BOPP manufacturing detail is outside knowledge without a named dated source.

decisions.decision: Do not flag narration length.
decisions.reason: Timing is checked separately by BIE.

uncertain: No page images were supplied; source fidelity is assessed against the task card's extracts.

problems.problem: Interoperability issues are named and interoperability is defined, but the payment problem itself is not opened. The learner never sees how incompatible systems prevent or complicate a transfer and thereby motivate seeking an alternative.
problems.fix: Add one hypothetical sentence showing a customer unable to pay a merchant because their systems cannot exchange the instruction, followed by the resulting inconvenience. Fund this by shortening b74–b75 or the repeated crypto-status recap in b59.

problems.problem: The explanation that biaxial orientation involves stretching the film in two directions is an examinable outside manufacturing fact, but no dated source is named.
problems.fix: Attach a suitable named, dated source to this beat. No additional narration is necessary.

checklist.note: Book claims and hypothetical examples are generally distinguished; the questionable purchasing-power claim is qualified.
The interoperability grievance still needs its practical mechanism.
Notes provide purpose, questions, decisions and an uncertainty field.
Language is predominantly natural spoken Hinglish.
Interoperability issues are compressed into naming and definition.
The practical consequence of incompatible payment systems is not explained.
Numerical mechanisms and statement traps generally suit UPSC/PCS learners.
Timing is code-managed; the wider prerequisite video and chapter plan are not supplied.
Most coverage is substantive, but one source grievance remains underdeveloped.
No extended prerequisite recap or obvious prerequisite dependency gap.
Hindi uses Devanagari and English terms remain Roman.
b70's coverage of interoperability issues is stronger in its claim than its teaching.
The compatibility-related causal chain lacks its operative link.
Interoperability needs an everyday payment failure and consequence, not merely its meaning.
Core economic mechanisms generally receive numerical examples before their formal names.
Numerical stories generally describe events rather than reading state-change notation.
b26 lacks dated attribution for its outside manufacturing fact.
Narration teaches facts without pointing learners to book pages or figures.
